hook: SCP-914 is a room-sized clockwork machine with an intake booth, an output booth, and a dial with five settings from Rough to Very Fine. Before reading the test log, try guessing what each setting would do to something ordinary, then check your guesses. Note the warning near the top banning biological tests; the article will show you why.
whyItMatters:
914 is a pure input-and-output premise, and it practically asks the reader to design their own experiments. The article leans into that openly: its closing note invites any qualified researcher to run mundane, non-living tests and points to a separate experiment log for the results, so the file reads as the start of an ongoing project rather than a finished report.

It is also a clean example of how much an SCP can do with a test log alone, with almost no narrative around it.
thingsToNotice:
The steel tests build like a joke: Rough gives laser-cut chunks, 1:1 gives screws, Fine gives carpet tacks, and Very Fine gives a gram of an impossible metal that can't be bent and conducts almost perfectly. The everyday items are funnier and stranger, since 'refinement' means a watch taken fully apart, a phone swapped for a different model, or a white mouse returned brown. A revolver on Very Fine produces something redacted that disintegrates everything in its line of fire.

Then the living tests turn grim. One chimp comes out of Rough as a crushed, heat-cut corpse; a D-class put through 1:1 emerges as a different man, confused and violent, and is shot. The Very Fine subject breaks out, kills eight guards and both researchers, causes three other containment breaches, wipes part of the response team's memories, and finally dissolves into blue ash that blinds the people nearby. The log answers that with a single line ending biological testing, and the flat tone makes it hit harder.
